      We easily observe that the descent data on ⟦19⟧ for ⟦20⟧ (given here by the actions of the Galois group ⟦21⟧ of ⟦22⟧ over ⟦23⟧) is not effective, since the group permutes certain doubled points (so that there are orbits that are not contained in an affine open).
      However, Mumford has shown that, if ⟦24⟧ is a separable projective morphism such that, for all ⟦25⟧, the irreducible components of ⟦26⟧ are geometrically irreducible with respect to ⟦27⟧, then ⟦28⟧ exists;
      the proof relies on a refinement of his theorem of passage to the quotient, cf. [Mumford–Tate seminar, 1962].
      Note also that it is still possible that, without any hypotheses on the irreducible components of the fibres ⟦29⟧, the scheme ⟦30⟧ (which will be introduced below) still exists.
